title: WSL2 MPS / driver mismatch - debugging journal
body:
TL;DR: Intermittent GPU initialization failures from containers running in WSL2 after recent Windows update. Symptoms look like a driver vs userland/runtime mismatch (host driver ok; WSL/container libs disagree). Also saw MPS-related failures when launching multiple worker processes. This doc is a running scratchpad of commands I ran, raw error lines, hypotheses, and next steps.

Environment checks (host + WSL):
- Windows 11 22H2, GPU: RTX A5000, NVIDIA driver: 535.86 (installed via .exe)
- WSL2 kernel: 6.1.95 (wsl --status shows default distro Ubuntu-22.04)
- nvidia-container-toolkit: 1.11.0 inside container image; container base image: ubuntu:22.04 + CUDA 12.1 runtime libs
- Using docker-desktop WSL2 backend, docker engine 24.0.5

Steps/commands run (chronological):
1) On Windows host: nvidia-smi
   -> Looks normal: Driver Version: 535.86, CUDA Version: 12.1
2) Inside WSL shell (ubuntu): sudo apt update; sudo apt install nvidia-utils-535 -y
   -> apt reported nvidia-utils-535 already present (from distro repo).
3) In WSL: nvidia-smi
   -> SUCCESS: shows same driver and GPU counters. So host<->WSL driver bridge is present.
4) Run a simple container: docker run --rm --gpus all --runtime=nvidia nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
   -> FAILURE (intermittent): container exits with 1 and log: "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Make sure that the latest NVIDIA driver is installed and running."
   -> Sometimes it works. This flakiness is the key symptom.

Container logs and error snippets captured:
- nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: driver error: failed to process request: unknown error
- libnvidia-container: get_driver_capabilities: cuda: driver/library version mismatch
- Container stdout: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" (from simple CUDA hello world compiled with cuda-runtime 12.1)
- When running many worker processes (3+), observed: "MPS server refused connection (errno=111)" inside container process logs
- Occasionally saw: "cuInit(0) failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN" from pytorch startup

Commands to introspect inside failing container (when I managed to get a shell):
- ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so*
- readlink -f /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12
- ldconfig -p | grep -i nvidia
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version  (works in WSL host, not always present inside the container)

What I've tried so far (with notes):
- Reboot Windows + wsl --shutdown + docker desktop restart: reduced occurrences for ~2 hours, then flakiness returned. Suggests transient state rather than config file corruption.
- Reinstalled NVIDIA driver on Windows (clean install): no change long-term.
- Rolled back to 530.xx driver on host: brief improvement but flakiness resumed.
- Disabled docker image cache, pulled fresh nvidia/cuda:12.1-base image. Same result.
- Switched container CUDA runtime tag to 12.0 and 11.8 (older): older runtime images show fewer errors but still nonzero failure rate. Points to mismatch window between driver and in-container runtime.
- Turned off MPS (unset CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY, don't launch mps server): reduced "MPS server refused connection" but didn't fix driver/library mismatch errors.
- Ran strace on one failing container startup: saw early dlopen failures on /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 with error "file too short/invalid ELF" in one case (suspicious).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Windows update changed some kernel-level WSL/driver glue that sometimes returns inconsistent handles to the container runtime; results in device node temporarily unavailable -> intermittent nvidia-container-cli init failures.
2) Nvidia container toolkit (host component from Docker Desktop) and in-container CUDA runtime versions occasionally disagree in ways that surface as "driver/library version mismatch" when the host loader proxies calls from inside container to host driver. Race conditions during driver handshake cause flakiness under load.
3) MPS (multi-process server) is not fully supported through the WSL<->container boundary; attempts to start/attach MPS across container boundaries cause "refused connection" and then leave stale sockets which subsequent processes hit.
4) Corrupt symlink or broken libnvidia* files copied into container image at build time (observed one dlopen corrupt file case). Some CI build step may have packaged host libs inadvertently.

Quick reproducer script (to run repeatedly to catch flake):
for i in $(seq 1 50); do \n  docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash nvidia/cuda:12.1-base -c 'nvidia-smi -L && python -c "import torch; torch.cuda.device_count(); print(\"OK\")"' || echo "FAILED at iteration $i";\n  sleep 2;\ndone

Notes from debug outputs:
- /proc/driver/nvidia/version on host: contains driver 535.86 with build date matching Windows driver installer.
- Running the same docker command from plain Linux VM with same driver + container image never reproduces the failure -> strongly suggests WSL-specific interaction.
- dmesg in WSL sometimes contains: "nvidia: failed to init channel 0: -110" around times of failure.

Next steps I plan to try:
- Capture full nvidia-container-cli -v  --debug output in failing start and attach here.
- Instrument a loop that collects host nvidia-smi -q, wsl --status, and docker ps logs timestamps to correlate failure windows.
- Try updating docker-desktop to latest stable edge that includes newer nvidia toolkit shim.
- Build a minimal container that does NOT include any CUDA libraries (uses host-provided) to see if in-container runtime libs are the cause. If that stabilizes, problem is in-container runtime mismatch.
- Check Windows event viewer for any nvlddmkm or WSL driver warnings around the timestamps.
- Ask SRE to reproduce on another WSL2 machine with same Windows update patch level.

Notes/TODO (meta):
- If we confirm WSL2/driver glue is culprit, open upstream issue with WSL team (link in linked_artifacts) and escalate with NVIDIA if driver handshake logs show a driver-side error code.
- Clean up any stale MPS sockets (/tmp/nvidia-mps/*) on container teardown so next starts are not impacted.

Scratchpad/raw snippets captured: 
"nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: driver error: failed to process request: unknown error"
"libnvidia-container: get_driver_capabilities: cuda: driver/library version mismatch"
"CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version"
"MPS server refused connection (errno=111)"
"cuInit(0) failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN"

If someone else picks this up: start with the quick reproducer loop above, try switching to container image without any libcuda in /usr/local/cuda, and gather the nvidia-container-cli debug traces when it fails. Also attach host-side 'nvidia-smi -q -x' output from the same timestamps.

End of notes (for now).

-- Priya
